question: What is the main difference between laws and ethics in nursing practice?

options.A: Laws set the minimum legal boundaries while ethics guide moral excellence
options.B: Ethics carry prison sentences while laws only result in job loss
options.C: Ethics are written by parliament while laws are created by hospitals
options.D: Laws apply only to doctors while ethics apply only to nurses

explanation: Laws establish mandatory rules with legal penalties, whereas ethics provide a moral framework for striving toward fair and compassionate care. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T8#GNS216_U1_T8_h1)

question: Why do nurses need to understand both the law and professional ethics?

options.A: To bypass the need for patient consent during emergencies
options.B: To avoid breaking the law while giving kind, respectful care
options.C: To ensure hospitals never face financial audits
options.D: To successfully prosecute patients who break hospital rules

explanation: Knowing both legal rules and ethical principles protects you from trouble while making sure your patients always feel respected and cared for! [learn more](GNS216_U1_T8#GNS216_U1_T8_h1)

question: Which ethical principle is all about actively doing good and helping your patient?
explanation: Think of Beneficence as your active duty to do good and boost the health and well-being of everyone in your care. You've got this! [learn more](GNS216_U1_T8#GNS216_U1_T8_h2)

question: A pregnant patient decides to refuse a treatment you recommended. You respect her choice. Which principle are you showing?
explanation: Autonomy is all about respecting a patient's right to make their own informed choices about their body. Their health, their say! [learn more](GNS216_U1_T8#GNS216_U1_T8_h2)

question: Which two major legal codes deal with criminal law across Nigeria?

options.C: Family Law and Sharia Supreme Act

explanation: In Nigeria, the Criminal Code is used in the southern states while the Penal Code covers the northern states. Both handle serious legal offenses! [learn more](GNS216_U1_T8#GNS216_U1_T8_h3)

question: Why might health policies and laws look a bit different depending on which Nigerian state you are working in?

options.A: Due to regional differences in laws, culture, and state-level guidelines
options.B: Because nurses are only permitted to follow international laws
options.C: Because the federal government has no ministries dedicated to health
options.D: Due to a complete lack of any written healthcare policies in the country

explanation: Nigeria's federal system means local cultures and state laws can influence how national health guidelines are put into practice. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T8#GNS216_U1_T8_h3)

question: What are the three core ingredients needed for valid informed consent?

options.A: Payment of all hospital bills in advance
options.B: Written signature from the village head and husband
options.C: Voluntary agreement, full information, and mental capacity
options.D: Verbal agreement witnessed by two police officers

explanation: For consent to be valid, the patient must agree freely, understand the risks and benefits, and be mentally capable of making the choice. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T8#GNS216_U1_T8_h4)

question: An adult female patient refuses a procedure, but her husband insists you must do it anyway. What should you do?

options.A: Discharge the patient immediately without explanation
options.B: Obey the husband because he is the head of the household
options.C: Respect the patient's autonomous refusal and maintain her confidentiality
options.D: Perform the procedure secretly without the patient knowing

explanation: Every competent adult has the final say over her own body. A patient's right to refuse always overrides outside family demands. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T8#GNS216_U1_T8_h4)

question: Under most Nigerian laws, what is the main legal exception that allows for an abortion?

options.A: If the family cannot afford a child
options.C: If the pregnancy occurs during school term
options.D: To save the life of the pregnant woman

explanation: Nigerian law is very strict regarding abortion, but saving the mother's life is recognized as a legal exception. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T8#GNS216_U1_T8_h5)

question: A patient comes to the emergency ward bleeding heavily from an unsafe abortion. What is your immediate priority?

options.A: Provide immediate lifesaving emergency care to stabilize the patient
options.B: Report the patient to the police before offering any medical treatment
options.C: Wait for a court order before administering intravenous fluids
options.D: Refuse care based on personal moral objections to abortion

explanation: Saving a life always comes first! As a nurse, your duty is to stabilize and treat your patient in an emergency, no matter the circumstances. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T8#GNS216_U1_T8_h5)

question: What is a major ethical debate surrounding Assisted Reproductive Technology (ART) like IVF?

options.A: Guaranteed elimination of all genetic diseases at birth
options.B: Compulsory fertility treatment for all citizens
options.C: Fair access and what to do with unused embryos
options.D: Total absence of any legal regulations worldwide

explanation: ART often raises tough questions about fairness in who can afford it and how leftover embryos should be handled ethically. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T8#GNS216_U1_T8_h6)

question: Why is clear, informed consent so important before a couple starts IVF treatment?

options.A: Because nurses are legally required to adopt any resulting children
options.B: Because it prevents patients from ever experiencing natural conception again
options.C: Because decisions must be made early about storing or donating leftover embryos
options.D: Because IVF is completely illegal under all Nigerian federal statutes

explanation: Since IVF creates extra embryos, couples must agree in advance on what will happen to them to avoid future legal and emotional conflicts. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T8#GNS216_U1_T8_h6)

question: What usually stops teenagers from visiting clinics for reproductive health issues?

options.A: Mandatory free distribution of supplies in schools
options.B: A complete absence of hospitals in urban centers
options.C: Fear of being judged and a lack of privacy from staff
options.D: Strict laws requiring adolescent doctors for teenage patients

explanation: Teens often avoid seeking help because they are scared healthcare workers will gossip, judge them, or break their trust. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T8#GNS216_U1_T8_h7)

question: How does promising strict privacy change how teenagers use reproductive health services?

options.A: It guarantees that teenagers will never experience health complications
options.B: It completely replaces the need for parental guidance at home
options.C: It encourages teens to seek early advice, testing, and care
options.D: It legally forces parents to abandon their teenage children

explanation: When teens know their visit is confidential, they feel safe enough to get timely checkups, contraception, or treatment when they need it. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T8#GNS216_U1_T8_h7)

question: What do we call a nurse's ability to understand and respect a patient's cultural beliefs while giving great care?
explanation: Cultural competence helps you bridge cultural and religious gaps so you can care for your patients safely and respectfully. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T8#GNS216_U1_T8_h8)

question: Which of these is NOT something a nurse should do when dealing with harmful traditional practices?

options.A: Performing the harmful traditional practice to please community elders
options.B: Offering supportive counseling to women resisting the practice
options.C: Providing respectful health education on the dangers involved
options.D: Reporting illegal procedures or child abuse to the right authorities

explanation: As a nurse, your first loyalty is to your patient's safety. You should never take part in harmful traditional practices, no matter the local pressure! [learn more](GNS216_U1_T8#GNS216_U1_T8_h8)

question: What is one of the main goals of a nurse acting as a patient advocate in reproductive health?

options.A: Prosecuting doctors who violate hospital budgets
options.B: Writing new national criminal codes in parliament
options.C: Protecting patient rights and pushing for fair access to safe care
options.D: Setting insurance premiums for fertility clinics

explanation: As an advocate, you stand up for your patients' rights, fight against unfair treatment, and help them access the care they deserve. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T8#GNS216_U1_T8_h9)

question: You notice low-income women at the antenatal clinic aren't getting family planning info. What is the best advocacy action?

options.A: Working with the team to set up clear education sessions for all patients
options.B: Telling the affected patients to find a different hospital on their own
options.C: Ignoring the issue because it's not bedside nursing work
options.D: Reporting the patients to hospital management for asking questions

explanation: Good advocacy means speaking up and working with your team to make sure every single patient gets equal access to health information. Great job! [learn more](GNS216_U1_T8#GNS216_U1_T8_h9)
